advices.diagnosis: The Customer class has a high LCOM4 of 4, indicating low cohesion: each method accesses a distinct private attribute, so the method‑attribute graph has many disconnected components. The class has no dependencies on other internal classes (DCC=0) and all attributes are private (DAM=1.0). The design is essentially a data holder with accessor methods, which inflates the method count (NOM=5) and cyclomatic complexity (WMC=5) without providing meaningful behavior.

suggestions.title: Split Customer into smaller cohesive classes

advices.risk_notes: Splitting the class increases the number of classes and inter‑class references, which may raise DCC further and add maintenance overhead. Existing code that expects a single Customer object will need to be updated to use the new composition, and tests may break if they rely on the original API.
